We put up with our front large burner not having the ability to go below 3, which is the low/simmer setting for about a year which seems ridiculous now because replacing the infinite switch could not be easier.
After I disconnected the stove all it took was 6 screws to remove the back of the stove, 2 screws hold the switch in place, and 2 plastic harnesses hold the wires that connect to the contacts.
$20 switch, 2 day delivery, and 10 minutes to replace and we can simmer sauces on the front burner again.

It you didn't know, this oven switch fails because it is not able to handle the amps from the large burners. Small burners do not have this problem.

I've had to replace this switch twice since I've owned my stove, and it has more to do with the design of the stove than the switch.  This is the switch that sits right above the oven vent, so it is more subject to heat and steam coming from that vent, and over time, the contacts just seem to wear out faster, and you can actually start hearing the arching when the contacts are opening and closing.  Anyway, as I mentioned before, this is an exact replacement for the switch that was in the stove, and it was a simple replacement.

My husband, the daily coffee drinker, is new to the Keurig experience. We are pretty frugal, by choice, and we just couldn't justify the cost of the Kerrigan coffee brewer and those expensive k-cups.  A friend of ours recently upgraded her Keurig machine and gave us her old one. However, we still couldn't justify the costs of the k-cups. Then I found a fill your own k-cup alternative, so we started using them. We cut our coffee costs by half or more, we startes using 1.5 scoops of coffee each day as opposed to 3. My husband loved this, but I kept finding finely ground coffee bean particles at the bottom of my coffee  cup.  Then, I ran across these filters and they are the perfect solution for us.  We have cut our costs again. By using these filters, it causes the water to flow slower through the fill your own k-cup. This makes the coffee stronger since it brews longer in the fill your own k-cup before being released into the coffee cup. Now we use half a scoop of coffee every day. Perfect solution to help us keep our costs down.
